message:
fix: lighten audit log list responses

## Summary

Closes #14.

This keeps the audit log list endpoint focused on lightweight summary rows by omitting request/response headers and bodies from GET /admin/audit. Full payloads remain available through the existing GET /admin/audit/{id} detail route, which the audit table now calls only when a row is expanded.

## Changes

- Add a summary query path for audit log list responses.
- Return total and has_more pagination metadata from GET /admin/audit.
- Cap requested audit list page size to avoid accidental very large responses.
- Lazy-load full audit entry details in the UI when a row expands.
- Add integration coverage that list responses omit payloads while detail responses preserve them.

## Validation

- go test -c -o /tmp/crabtrap-admin.test ./internal/admin
- go test -c -o /tmp/crabtrap-proxy.test ./internal/proxy
- go vet ./...
- /Users/nathanmetzger/go/bin/staticcheck ./...
- make build-web

Note: go test ./internal/admin is blocked locally because Testcontainers cannot find rootless Docker in this environment.
target_issue: internal/admin/pg_audit_reader.go: The `query` method (called by both `QuerySummaries` and `Query`) creates its own `context.Background()` and ignores the request context passed by callers. `Count` correctly accepts and uses a `context.Context` parameter, so HTTP request cancellation and deadlines apply to it. But `QuerySummaries` runs outside any deadline: if a client disconnects mid-flight, the database query continues until completion, holding a pgxpool connection. Under load, this can exhaust the connection pool.
notes: Under the DOSR policy, this documented finding requires reject (Jakub's pilot). PR title + description become the commit message.
